stories.headline: Cerberus Buys Airbus's US Satellite Factory, PHINIA Pays $160 Million for an Asia-Pacific Brake Business and International Paper Speeds Up a Spin-Off
stories.summary: Cerberus Capital Management agreed on 24 Nov to buy the US Space Systems business of Airbus U.S. Space & Defense, including a roughly 200,000 sq ft satellite plant in Merritt Island, Florida; terms were not disclosed and closing is expected by end-2026. Auto-parts maker PHINIA agreed on 25 Nov to pay about $160 million for FMP Group's operations in Australia, Thailand and Malaysia, which bring about $120 million of annual revenue and $23 million of adjusted EBITDA. International Paper rose 5.66% on 24 Nov after its board approved an accelerated spin-off of the DS Smith EMEA packaging business.
stories.market: Mid-sized carve-outs keep flowing even as megadeals dominate: index changes add a flow trade too, with SharkNinja replacing AES in the S&P 500 before the open on 2 Dec.

body: Cerberus is taking over Airbus's US satellite-manufacturing operation in Merritt Island, Florida, which opened in 2019. Neither side disclosed a price, and Airbus does not report the US arm's revenue separately; closing is subject to customary conditions.

PHINIA signed a definitive asset purchase agreement for FMP Group's Asia-Pacific business, gaining rights to the Bendix brand in Australia and some other regional markets. The roughly $160 million price is about seven times the expected $23 million of adjusted EBITDA; closing, expected in the first half of 2027, needs regulatory approval and confirmatory insolvency proceedings.
International Paper's board approved a faster separation of the European packaging operations it acquired with DS Smith, while keeping a minority stake; investors sent the shares up 5.66% on 24 Nov.

stories.headline: Deere Misses on Profit and Guides 2027 Below the Street, Yet the Stock Climbs 4.4% on Signs the Farm Slump Has Bottomed
stories.summary: Deere's fiscal fourth-quarter net income slipped 1% to $1.051 billion, or $3.89 a share, short of the roughly $4.01-4.05 analysts expected, it reported before the open on 25 Nov. Equipment net sales of $10.51 billion beat estimates of about $10.34-10.37 billion, and total net sales and revenues fell 2% to $12.115 billion. Deere guided fiscal 2027 net income to $4.50-5.25 billion, below the $5.91 billion LSEG consensus, a range that absorbs a $250-400 million one-off pension charge. The shares fell about 3% before the bell but closed up 4.44% (25 Nov close) as investors focused on a forecast 5-15% rebound in US and Canadian large-ag sales.
stories.market: The relief spread across farm machinery: CNH Industrial jumped 8.0% on 25 Nov, while grain traders Bunge (-8.6%) and ADM (-3.8%) had slid a day earlier (24 Nov). The move adds to the industrials-over-chips rotation that lifted the Dow above 50,000.

body: Deere's quarter to 1 November ended a run of six straight earnings beats: diluted EPS of $3.89 came in below consensus, which sources put between $4.01 and $4.05, while net income edged down from $1.065 billion a year earlier. Sales held up better than feared, with equipment net sales of $10.51 billion ahead of forecasts even as total net sales and revenues slipped 2% year on year to $12.115 billion.

The 2027 outlook was the headline number. Net income of $4.50-5.25 billion sits well under the $5.91 billion analysts had pencilled in (LSEG), although it includes an estimated $250-400 million non-cash charge from offering some US salaried retirees a lump-sum pension option. Financial services is expected to earn about $900 million.

By segment, Deere sees Production & Precision Agriculture sales up 5-15%, Small Agriculture & Turf roughly flat, and Construction & Forestry flat to up 10%, the latter helped by data-centre construction. By region it forecasts US and Canada large ag up 5-15%, Europe flat to down 5%, South America flat to up 5% and Asia about flat. CEO John May pointed to early signs of improvement in large agriculture, led by North America, while warning that farmers still face tight margins and volatile crop prices.
Tariffs remain a drag: Deere estimates about $1 billion of tariff costs in fiscal 2027 against $1.1 billion in the year just ended, and booked $383 million of tariff recoveries in fiscal 2026.

The shares reversed an early fall to close 4.44% higher on 25 Nov. Going into the report the stock had fallen for six straight sessions from 11 Nov and closed at $624.89 on 19 Nov, about 13% below its 52-week high of $721.22. A year ago it fell about 5.7% after a disappointing guide.

key_figures.note: vs $5.91bn LSEG consensus; incl. $250-400m pension charge

analysts.view: Notes Deere historically guides conservatively and reads the North America outlook as a sign sales bottomed in 2026.

detail.consensus: The Street expected about $5.91 billion of fiscal 2027 net income (LSEG); Deere's range tops out roughly 11% below that.

stories.headline: HP Rallies 11.5% After All as Investors Look Past the Cash-Flow Guide; Dividend Lifted to 31 Cents
stories.summary: HP shares closed up 11.49% on 25 Nov, a day after its fiscal fourth-quarter report, recovering from an after-hours swing that had wiped out an early 17% jump. The company beat with adjusted EPS of $0.83 against a $0.75 consensus and revenue up 9% to $16.0 billion against $15.4 billion expected. It raised its quarterly dividend to 31 cents a share, while its forecast of about $3 billion of current-quarter free cash flow trailed the $3.3 billion analysts sought.
stories.market: HPQ was the top S&P 500 gainer in a session where the index swung from a 3.2% intraday loss to close down 0.25%; Dell, which reported the same day, added a more modest 0.6% (25 Nov close).

body: HP's results on 24 Nov beat on both lines: adjusted EPS of $0.83 versus about $0.75 expected and revenue of $16.0 billion, up 9%, against a $15.4 billion consensus. The initial after-hours pop faded on a free-cash-flow outlook of about $3 billion for the current quarter, short of the $3.3 billion analysts targeted, and on worries over PC margins.

In regular trading on 25 Nov buyers returned. The board's dividend increase to 31 cents a share and a fiscal 2027 outlook that market commentators described as respectable helped the stock close 11.49% higher, making it the S&P 500's best performer on the day.
The rebound contrasts with the wider AI-hardware complex, where Nvidia, Micron, Lam Research and Sandisk all lost between about 4% and 6% the same day.

stories.headline: Ambarella Sinks 20% and Nutanix 15% as Weak Guidance and Memory Shortages Punish Tech Reporters
stories.summary: Ambarella fell 19.77% on 25 Nov after guiding fourth-quarter revenue to $70-75 million, far below estimates, as memory-chip shortages squeeze its customers; the stock had been down as much as 37% before the open. Nutanix dropped 15.19% after its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook came in under consensus and it announced its chief executive will leave. Autodesk slid 3.49% after its quarterly report and Workday was also lower (25 Nov closes).
stories.market: The misses landed on a day the Nasdaq traded as much as 4.6% lower before closing down 0.62% at 23,585.80 (25 Nov); semiconductor and software names with exposure to component costs remain the weakest links.

The shares were indicated down 37% before the open and finished 19.77% lower as the broader market recovered.
Nutanix lost 15.19% after a fiscal 2027 revenue forecast below consensus and news of its CEO's planned exit, adding a leadership question to a slower growth outlook.

Autodesk fell 3.49% after its results, and Workday also traded lower. The pattern matches the week's earlier reports from Analog Devices and HPE, where component shortages and margin pressure outweighed headline beats.

stories.headline: Dick's Jumps 15% and Abercrombie 20% on Beat-and-Raise Quarters, While Urban Outfitters Drops 10% on Soft Comparable Sales
stories.summary: Dick's Sporting Goods rose 14.59% on 24 Nov after third-quarter adjusted EPS of $1.94 beat the $1.41 FactSet estimate and revenue rose 23.2% to $5.13 billion; it lifted its full-year adjusted EPS outlook to $11.45-12.30 from $11-12. Abercrombie & Fitch gained 19.69% the same day on a beat and higher full-year guidance, then added 5.27% on 25 Nov despite a downgrade. Urban Outfitters fell 10.33% on 25 Nov after retail comparable sales of 4.4% missed the 5.3% estimate.
stories.market: Retail is splitting on execution rather than macro: the S&P MidCap 400 rose 1.23% on 25 Nov as money rotated from chips into consumer names, but misses are still punished hard.

body: Dick's beat comfortably: adjusted EPS of $1.94 against $1.41 expected and revenue up 23.2% to $5.13 billion versus about $5.08 billion consensus. It raised its full-year adjusted EPS range to $11.45-12.30 and disclosed $1 billion of new borrowing alongside $903 million of share repurchases.

stories.headline: Rémy Cointreau Leaps 10% on New Long-Term Targets as Prosus Slides to a 2½-Year Low; Siemens Energy India's Profit Rises 82%
stories.summary: Rémy Cointreau shares jumped 10.2% in Paris on 25 Nov after the cognac maker set new sales, profit and cash targets running to fiscal 2031/32 and raised its operating-margin outlook for the current year. Prosus fell 3.4% to its lowest in about two and a half years after weaker first-half operating profit. Sweden's Elekta rose as much as 12.5% on a second-quarter profit beat before paring gains, and Pets at Home hit a two-year high on its profit outlook. In India, Siemens Energy India's September-quarter net profit rose 81.5% to Rs 653 crore on revenue up 30.4% to Rs 3,453 crore.
stories.market: Luxury and spirits led the STOXX 600 higher on 25 Nov, with Swatch up 6% and Richemont 3%, while Prosus weighed on the internet-holding complex.

body: Rémy Cointreau's first-half operating profit came in ahead of expectations and the group laid out targets for sales, profit and cash generation through fiscal 2031/32, while lifting its operating-margin growth outlook for this year. The 10.2% gain made it one of the strongest European large caps on the day and pulled luxury names with it.
Prosus slipped 3.4% after a weaker first-half operating profit, leaving the technology investor at a roughly 2½-year low.

Elekta's second-quarter profit beat sent the radiotherapy-equipment maker up as much as 12.5% intraday before it settled around 2% higher. Pets at Home touched a two-year high after guiding profit toward the top of forecasts.

In Asia, Li Auto's quarterly loss of 0.12 yuan a share was narrower than expected and the stock rose more than 4% before the US open. Siemens Energy India, which reports on an October-September year, posted an 81.5% jump in quarterly profit to Rs 653 crore.

stories.headline: BofA and Barclays Upgrade Sanofi After the $41 Billion Insmed Deal, While Guggenheim and UBS Move Insmed to Neutral
stories.summary: Bank of America raised Sanofi to Buy from Neutral and lifted its target to €125 from €92 on 25 Nov, arguing the Insmed purchase could add about 20% to 2033 EPS and offset Dupixent's loss of exclusivity in 2031. Barclays moved to Overweight with a €120 target, up from €90, forecasting about $16 billion of peak sales from Insmed's drugs. Guggenheim and UBS cut Insmed to Neutral from Buy, effectively treating it as a deal-arbitrage stock, with Guggenheim seeing no higher bidder. Sanofi's US-listed shares added 4.80% (25 Nov close) after a 9.9% jump in Paris the day before.
stories.market: The upgrades extend Sanofi's rerating: Barclays argues for a move from 9 to 11.5 times 2028 earnings. Insmed now trades as a spread to the $175 cash price.

body: BofA's Sachin Jain expects Sanofi's 2027 EPS to grow about 11%, against roughly 7% consensus, and sees little risk the deal fails to close. He cautioned that Insmed does not fix Sanofi's research productivity problem.

Barclays' James Gordon raised his peak forecast for Dupixent to $36 billion and put Insmed's portfolio at about $16 billion of peak revenue, saying the faster growth profile deserves a higher multiple.

On the target side, Guggenheim's Vamil Divan and UBS both cut Insmed to Neutral from Buy; Guggenheim does not expect a rival offer. The $175-a-share cash deal, about 46% above Insmed's unaffected 18 Nov close, is expected to close in the first half of 2027 subject to shareholder and regulatory approval.

stories.headline: JPMorgan Cuts AB InBev to Neutral on 2027 Cost Inflation; GoodRx Sinks 21% on a Downgrade and Wedbush Starts Paychex at Outperform
stories.summary: JPMorgan's Celine Pannuti downgraded AB InBev to Neutral from Overweight and cut her target to €75 from €80 on 25 Nov, warning cost inflation will cap European staples in 2027; her top picks include Unilever, British American Tobacco, Nestlé and Carlsberg. GoodRx fell 20.67% after a downgrade, while Shoals Technologies rose 9.23% on an upgrade. Wedbush initiated Paychex at Outperform with a $134 target, lifting the stock 2.96%. stories.market: The AB InBev call frames 2027 positioning in European staples around food, tobacco and ingredients over brewers and soft drinks; AB InBev's US shares closed down 0.11% (25 Nov).

body: JPMorgan's staples team expects a mixed 2027 after a strong year for the sector, naming higher cost inflation as the biggest earnings risk. Pannuti removed AB InBev from the bank's Analyst Focus List, is cautious on soft-drink makers and more restrained on brewers, and favours food (excluding chocolate), tobacco, ingredients and cosmetics. Her 2027 top picks are Unilever, BAT, Nestlé, Puig, Kerry, Danone, Carlsberg and Reckitt.

In the US, GoodRx was the session's worst performer after a downgrade, losing 20.67%, while an upgrade sent Shoals Technologies up 9.23%. Wedbush's new Outperform rating and $134 target on Paychex added 2.96%.

Some downgrades failed to bite in a session dominated by rotation out of tech: Abercrombie rose 5.27% and HCA 1.92% despite cuts. In London, UBS lowered its rating on Marks & Spencer, whose shares stood at 452.30p.

stories.headline: S&P Puts Nvidia's AA Rating on Watch for a Cut Over Governance, as Moody's Holds at Aa1 as the Stock's November Loss Reaches 27%
stories.summary: S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's AA issuer and senior unsecured ratings on CreditWatch Negative on 25 Nov, citing management and governance risk after Jensen Huang resigned on 12 Nov and was reinstated on 23 Nov. S&P said any downgrade, likely by one notch, could come within 90 days, and lowered its governance assessment to neutral from positive. Moody's kept Nvidia at Aa1 with a stable outlook the same day. Nvidia shares closed down 3.91% on 25 Nov, after falling as much as 9% intraday, leaving them about 27% lower in November.
stories.market: A rare split between the two big agencies on the world's most valuable chipmaker; credit-risk gauges on Nvidia hit records this week, and the stock's slide is weighing on the Nasdaq and Asian chip markets.

body: S&P's concerns centre on the board: it questioned whether long-serving directors remain independent, and flagged weak oversight of the chief executive and the absence of a clear succession plan. Huang's departure and return within 11 days did not fully resolve those questions, the agency said.

S&P also said it would view negatively any finding of export-control violations or understated China disclosures. It stressed that Nvidia's competitive position, technology lead and balance sheet are unchanged, and that a cut would likely be one notch unless investigations show wider damage.
Moody's took a different line, affirming Aa1 with a stable outlook and saying Huang's return restores strategic continuity, while noting key-person risk and open governance issues.
The equity market is already pricing turmoil: Nvidia traded as much as 9% lower on 25 Nov before closing down 3.91%, and is down about 27% for the month.

stories.headline: Hedge Funds Pile Into ETF Shorts at One of the Fastest Paces in a Decade as Money Floods Into Large-Cap and Treasury ETFs
stories.summary: Hedge-fund short positions in ETFs rose about 19 percentage points in the past week, the third-largest weekly increase in a decade, Goldman Sachs' Vincent Lin said in remarks reported on 26 Nov. Funds had cut equity exposure for five straight weeks before switching to actively adding shorts in single stocks, index futures and ETFs, with positioning at multi-year lows. Longer-term investors went the other way: US large-cap blend ETFs took in $6.57 billion and long-dated Treasury ETFs $2.40 billion on 24 Nov, while thematic and disruptive-tech ETFs lost $1.54 billion and $1.35 billion.
stories.market: Light positioning raises the odds of sharp short-covering bounces like 25 Nov's late reversal, when the Dow erased a 1,100-point loss; the rotation favours staples, utilities, REITs and healthcare over tech and homebuilders.

body: According to Goldman's Vincent Lin, hedge funds spent five weeks reducing equity exposure before turning to outright shorting. The roughly 19-point weekly jump in ETF shorts ranks as the third-largest in ten years.

Funds are rotating out of high-volatility technology and adding shorts in consumer cyclicals, homebuilders in particular, while moving into staples, utilities and REITs. Lin remains positive on hyperscale data-centre operators and sees better value in healthcare than in staples.

Long-only money is still arriving: ETFs and mutual funds took in about $150 billion over the past month. Daily ETF data for 24 Nov showed inflows of $6.57 billion into US large-cap blend funds, $2.40 billion into long-term Treasury funds and $2.30 billion into technology sector funds, against outflows of $1.54 billion from thematic multi-sector, $1.35 billion from disruptive-tech and $887.1 million from US small-cap blend ETFs.
That mix of bearish fast money and steady real-money buying helped explain 25 Nov: the S&P 500 fell as much as 3.2% intraday before closing down just 0.25% at 7,182.78, and 370 of its members rose.

analysts.view: Positioning at multi-year lows; hedge funds rotating to defensives and shorting tech, consumer cyclicals and homebuilders; still constructive on hyperscale data-centre operators.

calendar.why: Wednesday's closes stand; liquidity in global markets thin, with Europe, India and Asia trading normally.

calendar.event: ECB: account of the October monetary policy meeting
calendar.why: Shows how far policymakers lean towards tightening, with inflation pressures building globally.
Prior readings 2.8% headline and 2.4% ex food and energy; a hot print would add to December BOJ hike bets after Tamura's call for faster hikes.
Tests corporate earnings as battery makers cut output and the US proposes up to 20% overcapacity tariffs.

calendar.event: France and Spain: preliminary November CPI
calendar.why: Early signal for euro-area inflation ahead of the flash estimate.

calendar.event: Black Friday: US half-day trading session
calendar.why: First US trading after Thanksgiving and the Section 301 proposals; read on holiday retail demand.
Output policy with Brent back near $95 on Red Sea and Hormuz attacks.

calendar.event: S&P Global: scheduled review of France's sovereign rating
calendar.why: A rating action would move OAT-Bund spreads and French banks.
Forecasts range from about 7% to 7.8%, against 7.8% in Q1; feeds the RBI's 4 Dec decision.

calendar.event: Nvidia: Jensen Huang's closed-door interviews with House committees
calendar.why: First congressional questioning since his reinstatement on 23 Nov; Nvidia shares remain volatile.

calendar.event: US Senate Banking Committee hearing with Jensen Huang on AI export controls
calendar.why: Public testimony on chip diversion concerns linked to Megaspeed, newly placed on the Entity List.

calendar.event: India: RBI Monetary Policy Committee decision
calendar.why: Most economists expect a 25 bp hike after October CPI rose to 6.1% and RBI staff flagged broadening inflation.
